guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Paediatric Basic Life Support 2021 (Choking)
title: Child choking on a button at a country show
setting: County show treatment centre. A father runs in holding his 8-year-old daughter. She is gasping, clutching at her throat, and unable to speak.
verdictExplanation: Severe complete paediatric airway obstruction (unable to speak, cough, or breathe). Choking is a critical life-threatening emergency. Sick: deliver paediatric choking treatment.

shared.response: Responding to voice with severe panic

history.history: Chewing a plastic button off her jumper, accidentally swallowed it and started choking
history.drugs: Allergic to peanuts, has an EpiPen (not indicated here)
history.injuries: None visible, reports back and chest pain from gasping

followUp.question: What is the correct protocol for treating a conscious child with severe choking?

options.text: Lean her forward, give up to 5 back blows; if unsuccessful, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts; repeat
Perform adult abdominal thrusts with full strength while she stands upright
Give her peanut allergy EpiPen into her outer thigh immediately
Hold her upside down by her feet and slap her back vigorously

followUp.explanation: Paediatric conscious choking is managed with up to 5 back blows followed by up to 5 abdominal thrusts. The force must be adjusted for a child. EpiPen is only for anaphylaxis, not mechanical choking. Inverting the child is dangerous and wastes time.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Reassure father. Lean child forward and deliver 5 back blows, then 5 abdominal thrusts. Call 999 if the button does not clear.
levelFlags.erNotes: Deliver paediatric choking treatment. If she becomes unresponsive, immediately guide her to the floor, call 999, and start paediatric CPR (beginning with 5 rescue breaths, check mouth before breathing).
